title: Gold-Nanobeacons as a theranostic system for the detection and inhibition of specific genes
protocol: Prepare aqua regia by mixing 3:1 concentrated HCl:HNO3 in a large open container in a fume hood.
Immerse the 500 ml two-neck flask, magnetic stir bar, stopper, condenser, and a 250 mL Erlenmeyer in freshly prepared aqua regia for at least 15 min.
Wash the glassware with copious amounts of Millipore-filtered water.
Load 225 mL of 1 mM HAuCl4 into the rounded bottom two-neck flask.
Place the stirrer inside the flask, connect the condenser to one neck of the flask, and place the stopper in the other neck.
Put the flask on the hot plate to reflux while stirring.
When the solution begins to reflux, remove the stopper and swiftly add 25 ml of 38.8 mM (285 mg) sodium citrate.
Place the stopper back into the two-neck flask.
Allow the system to reflux for another 30 min.
Turn off heating and allow the system to cool down to room temperature under stirring.
Keep the system protected from light.
Transfer the colloidal solution to a 250 mL Erlenmeyer amber flask with a ground glass cap.
Take a UV-Visible spectrum of the AuNPs.
Characterize the produced AuNPs by Transmission Electron Microscopy.
Determine the nanoparticles’ concentration via Lambert–Beer equation.
Use the absorbance and the molar absorptivity of the nanoparticles for calculation.
Expect a typical Surface Plasmon Resonance peak at around 520 nm with an extinction coefficient of ~2.33×108 M-1.cm-1.
Normal production yields a solution of gold nanoparticles in the range of 13 to 15 nM.
Ensure the absorbance does not exceed 2 to avoid deviations from the Lambert–Beer law.
Dilute the sample if the measured absorbance exceeds this value and adjust for dilution factor when calculating original stock concentration.
Store prepared nanoparticles stably for months in a container, preferably glass treated with aqua regia, at room temperature.
Do not freeze the nanoparticles.
Mix 41.7 mL of a 12 nM stock solution of citrate-gold nanoparticles with 150 µL of a 1 mg/mL stock solution of O-(2-Mercaptoethyl)-O’-methyl-hexa(ethylene glycol) (PEG).
Incubate for 10 minutes.
Add 625 µL of a 2 M stock solution of NaOH to reach a final concentration of 25 mM.
Incubate for 16 hours at room temperature.
Distribute the volume in centrifuge tubes and centrifuge at 21,460 ×g for 30 min at 4ºC to remove excess PEG.
Remove the supernatant and keep it for subsequent analysis while tracking the removed volume.
Resuspend the precipitate by adding DEPC-treated water.
Run an UV-Visible spectrum of the PEGylated AuNPs and determine the concentration using the same method as described in step 7.
Prepare a calibration curve in the range of 0.0002-0.035 mg/mL of PEG.
Mix the appropriate amount of stock solution of PEG for each concentration with 100 µL of phosphate buffer 0.5 M (pH 7).
Add Milli-Q water up to 300 µL.
Mix 200 µL of the supernatant retrieved in step 9 with 100 µL of phosphate buffer 0.5 M (pH 7).
Add 7 µL of 0.05 mg/mL 5,5’-dithio-bis-(2-nitrobenzoic acid) (DNTB) to each mixture.
Incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Take a UV-Visible absorption spectrum from 290 to 600 nm of each mixture.
Record absorbance values at 412 nm.
Use the calibration curve to calculate PEG amount in the supernatant.
Subtract calculated PEG value from the added amount to determine bonded PEG molecules on AuNPs’ surface.
Store nanoparticles functionalized with O-(2-Mercaptoethyl)-O'-methyl-hexa(ethylene glycol) at 4°C for up to 6 months in darkness.
Mix thiolated oligonucleotides with DTT to achieve a final concentration of 0.1 M.
Incubate the mixture for at least 2 hours at 4°C.
Extract one volume (100-500 μL) of thiol-modified oligonucleotide with two volumes of ethyl acetate.
Mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 21,460 × g.
Discard the organic phase (upper phase).
Repeat steps to extract and centrifuge the mixture two more times.
Purify the remaining aqueous phase using a desalting NAP-5 column according to manufacturer instructions.
Use 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH 8) as eluent.
Quantify the purified oligonucleotide by UV-Visible spectroscopy using the extinction coefficient at 260 nm.
Mix the purified oligonucleotide with PEGylated AuNPs in a 1:100 AuNP:oligonucleotide ratio.
Add AGE I solution to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 8, and 0.01% w/v SDS.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Sequentially increase the ionic strength by adding AGE II up to a final concentration of 10 mM phosphate buffer, pH 8, 0.05 M NaCl, and 0.01% w/v SDS.
Incubate for 20 minutes after each addition.
Repeat step with final concentrations of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 M of NaCl.
Incubate for 16 hours at room temperature following the last addition.
Centrifuge for 20 minutes at 21,460 × g.
Remove a fixed amount of supernatant and store it.
Redisperse the precipitate in the same volume of DEPC-treated water.
Repeat step centrifuging two more times.
Take a UV-Visible spectrum of the Au-nanobeacons.
Determine the concentration using the method described previously.
Prepare a calibration curve in the range of 0.1-10 µmol of oligonucleotide added in step 20.
Mix appropriate amounts of fluorescent oligonucleotide stock solution with AGE I and AGE II solutions to obtain a final volume of 100 µL.
Ensure the final concentration is 10 mM phosphate buffer (pH 8), 0.3 M NaCl, and 0.01% (w/v) SDS.
Prepare a second calibration curve in the range of 0.1-2.5 µmol of oligonucleotide added in step 19.
Mix appropriate amounts of fluorescent oligonucleotide stock solution with DEPC-treated water to obtain a final volume of 100 µL.
Use at least 5 different concentrations to build your calibration curve.
Take fluorescence spectra of each mixture of the calibration curve and the supernatants recovered in previous steps.
Excite the fluorophore at 490 nm, collect emission at 500-700 nm with 5 nm slits for 6-FAM.
Calculate the area under the curve from the emission spectra.
Use the equation of the calibration curve to determine the amount of fluorophore-labelled oligonucleotides in each supernatant.
Subtract the result from the amount of oligonucleotides added previously to obtain the amount present at the surface.
Determine the final AuNP:oligonucleotides ratio using the obtained value.
Fully characterize the Au-nanobeacons by determining the hydrodynamic radius with Dynamic Light Scattering.
Determine the surface charge through Zeta Potential.
Store Au-nanobeacons at 4°C in the dark for 3 months.
Incubate 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons in phosphate buffer (10 mM, pH 8) at increasing temperatures from 10ºC to 80ºC.
Take an emission spectrum at the wavelength appropriate to the chosen fluorophore every 2 minutes.
Calculate the area under each spectrum curve and plot results against temperature.
Incubate 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons in phosphate buffer (10 mM, pH 8) at decreasing temperatures from 80ºC to 10ºC.
Take an emission spectrum at the wavelength appropriate to the chosen fluorophore every 2 minutes.
Calculate the area under each spectrum curve and plot results against temperature.
Incubate 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with 5 mM, 10 mM, and 100 mM DTT at 37°C for 24 hours.
Measure fluorescence intensity at 37°C every 15 minutes using appropriate excitation and emission setups for the chosen fluorophore.
Incubate 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with 5 mM, 10 mM, and 100 mM glutathione at 37°C for 24 hours.
Measure fluorescence intensity at 37°C every 15 minutes using appropriate excitation and emission setups for the chosen fluorophore.
Mix 1 nM of Au-nanobeacons with complementary and non-complementary targets.
Add 20 µL of transcription buffer 5× to achieve a final volume of 100 µL.
Ensure an amount of target molecules at least five times the corresponding amount of oligonucleotides functionalized into the AuNPs for each sequence.
Incubate the Au-nanobeacon with complementary and non-complementary single-stranded nucleic acid molecules at 37°C for 2 hours in transcription buffer.
Record the emission spectra of the Au-nanobeacons periodically, every 2 minutes if real-time measurement is desired.
If only the final result is important, record the fluorescence spectrum at the end.
Calculate the area under each spectrum and plot it against the variable being studied, such as time or amount of template.
Create a calibration curve with increasing amounts of non-complementary and complementary target from 0 to 2000 µg.

Mix 1 nM of Au-nanobeacon with fluorescently-labelled complementary oligonucleotide in phosphate buffer 10 mM (pH 8) for a final volume of 200 µL, ensuring at least 7 different concentrations of complementary fluorescently-labelled oligonucleotides are prepared.
Heat the mixtures at 80°C for 10 minutes.
Slowly cool down the mixtures to 20°C with controlled temperature decrease of 0.1°C/minute and stabilize at 20°C for at least 20 minutes.
Place 100 µL of the prepared mixtures in a Ultra-micro volume quartz fluorescence cuvette.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of the fluorophore on the Au-nanobeacon for each mixture using the appropriate spectrofluorimeter configuration.
Centrifuge the remaining 100 µL for 20 minutes at 21,460 ×g.
Recover 80 µL of the supernatants without disturbing the oily precipitate.
Redisperse the precipitate by adding 80 µL of phosphate buffer 10 mM \(pH 8).
Centrifuge the mixture again for 20 minutes at 21,460 ×g.
Recover 80 µL of the supernatant.
Prepare a calibration curve in the range of 1 nmol to 4 µmol of the fluorescently-labelled oligonucleotide by mixing appropriate amounts with phosphate buffer 10 mM \(pH 8).
Measure the fluorescence intensity of the tubes in the calibration curve and of the supernatants recovered in previous steps.
Calculate the area under the curve of the emission spectra.
Determine the amount of fluorophore-labelled oligonucleotides present in each supernatant using the equation of the calibration curve.
Subtract the result from the amount of oligonucleotides added in step 34a for each tube.
Use the determined value to ascertain the amount of targets hybridized to the Au-nanobeacons for each concentration.
Plot the fluorescence intensity measured in step 34c versus the amount of hybridized target molecules.

Prepare an in vitro transcription reaction consisting of 20 µL of Transcription buffer 5×, reporter Au-nanobeacon for final concentration of 1 nM, 10 mM of each NTP and 0.6 µg of DNA template in a final volume of 100 µL.
Incubate the transcription reaction for 30 min at 37°C.
Record the emission spectra of the corresponding fluorophore using appropriate excitation and emission conditions.
Record the emission every 2 minutes during incubation.
Quickly add 30 U of T7 RNA polymerase to the reaction mixture.
Continue recording the fluorescence of the reaction every 2 minutes after adding the enzyme.
Prepare an in vitro transcription reaction with 20 µL of Transcription buffer 5×.
Add reporter Au-nanobeacon for a final concentration of 1 nM.
Add inhibitor Au-nanobeacon for a final concentration of 1 nM.
Include 10 mM of each NTP and 0.6 µg of DNA template in a final volume of 100 µL.
Incubate the reaction mixture for 30 min at 37°C.
Record the emission spectra of the corresponding fluorophore using appropriate excitation and emission conditions every 2 minutes.
Quickly add 30 U of T7 RNA polymerase to the incubating solution.
Continue recording fluorescence of the reaction every 2 minutes during enzyme addition.
Incubate for an additional hour and 30 minutes at 37°C after adding the enzyme.
Seed 1×10^5 cells/well in 24-well plates the day before EGFP plasmid transfection, using antibiotic-free complete growth medium.
Check cell density with an inverted optical microscope.
Detach cells with trypsin 1x and resuspend them in complete growth medium, antibiotic-free.
Pellet cells by mild centrifugation at 250 ×g for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL of complete growth medium, antibiotic-free.
Incubate cells at 37°C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere for 24 hours.
Aspirate the medium in each well and immediately add 400 μl of fresh Opti-MEM® I Reduced Serum Medium to each well.
Dilute 2 μl of Lipofectamine Reagent in 48.5 μl of serum-free medium and incubate 5 minutes at room temperature.
Dilute 1 µg of EGFP vector in 45 μL of serum-free medium and incubate 5 minutes at room temperature.
Mix solutions together gently by pipetting up and down and flicking the tube.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Add 100 μL of DNA vector-Lipofectamine complexes to each well.
Mix gently by rocking the plate back and forth.
Incubate the cells at 37°C in a CO2 incubator for 24 hours.
Incubate cells with 30 nM of antisense Au-nanobeacons for EGFP silencing in Opti-MEM® Reduced Serum Medium.
Shake well to ensure even distribution of nanoparticles in the well.
After 24 hours of EGFP vector transfection, check EGFP expression using an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Incubate cells with a titration series of hairpin oligonucleotide functionalized on NPs’ surface concentrations for EGFP silencing.
Wash cells with 500 μL of 1× PBS after 24 to 72 hours.
Assess knockdown by extracting total RNA and using it for real-time RT-PCR or measuring EGFP fluorescence from cell lysates.
Lyse cells with osmotic shock by incubating in 100 µl of water.
Briefly sonicate the cells for 5 minutes.
Pipette the cell lysate several times and vortex to ensure sufficient disruption.
Keep lysates on ice.
Centrifuge cell lysates at 20,000 ×g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Remove tubes from the centrifuge.
Recover supernatants after ensuring they are clear.
Measure fluorescence using 100 µL of supernatant in a spectrofluorimeter with quartz cuvette (EGFP: Excitation/Emission = 480/510 nm).
Measure fluorescence emission by taking the area under the curve from 495 to 650 nm.
Perform a Bradford assay to determine total protein concentrations of each sample.
Normalize EGFP fluorescence values to bulk protein concentration using a standard calibration curve of protein (e.g., BSA).
Determine percent knockdown of EGFP by normalizing normalized fluorescence values for each sample to untreated controls.
Fix cells with 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS for 15 min at 37°C after step 11.
Mount cell on coverslip in a slide using 20 μL of ProLong® Gold Antifade Reagent with DAPI for nuclear staining.
Image cells with a confocal laser point-scanning microscope, using 405 nm excitation for DAPI (nucleus), 480 nm for EGFP, and 561 nm for Cy3 (recommended dye for Au-nanobeacons).
Repeat steps 36-49.
Incubate cells with 10 nM of siRNA for EGFP using 2 μL of Lipofectamine 2000 and Opti-MEM® Reduced Serum Medium after 24 hours of EGFP vector transfection, as described in steps 6-8.

Add 10 nM (concentration of hairpin oligonucleotide functionalized on the NPs’ surface calculated in steps 24-29 of beacon coverage on AuNPs) of Anti-siRNA Au-nanobeacons in Opti-MEM® Reduced Serum Medium with several delays of incubation (0.5, 1, 3, 6 and 24 hours) regarding siRNA incubation.
Evaluate EGFP recovery after an optimal delay for maximal gene expression recovery, typically around 0.5-1 hours after the initial siRNA incubation.
Wear gloves.
After 48 hours, wash cells in 1× PBS.
Repeat steps 50-61.
Repeat steps 36-49.
Incubate cells with 30 nM of Antisense Au-nanobeacons for EGFP silencing in Opti-MEM® Reduced Serum Medium.
Shake well to ensure even distribution of nanoparticles in the well.

For evaluation of EGFP recovery, add 30 nM of ssRNA oligonucleotides against Antisense Au-nanobeacons in Opti-MEM® Reduced Serum Medium with several delays of incubation (0.5, 1, 3, 6 and 24 hours) regarding Antisense Au-nanobeacons incubation.
After 48 hours, wash cells in 1× PBS.
Repeat steps 50-61.
Plate cells at 1×10^5 cells/well in 24-well plates in the afternoon.
Treat cells with 10 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 24 hours.
Treat cells with 30 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 24 hours.
Treat cells with 50 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 24 hours.
Wash cells with 1× PBS after 24 hours of treatment.
Lysed and collect cells for RNA extraction or prepare for confocal microscopy after 24 hours of treatment.
Treat cells with 10 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 48 hours.
Treat cells with 30 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 48 hours.
Treat cells with 50 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 48 hours.
Wash cells with 1× PBS after 48 hours of treatment.
Lysed and collect cells for RNA extraction or prepare for confocal microscopy after 48 hours of treatment.
Treat cells with 10 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 72 hours.
Treat cells with 30 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 72 hours.
Treat cells with 50 nM of Anti-miR Au-nanobeacons for 72 hours.
Wash cells with 1× PBS after 72 hours of treatment.
Lysed and collect cells for RNA extraction or prepare for confocal microscopy after 72 hours of treatment.
